gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-kannada: Noto Sans Kannada is friendly and modern, with a gentle rise to capitals. Tilt Neon draws every stroke like bent wire at a constant width, and the body's s curves open generously at both ends.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-mayan-nume: Noto Sans Mayan Numerals stands tall, with a visibly gaping c. Tilt Neon above it holds a tube-like stroke that never varies, while the tall-bodied small letters below keep the text lean and upright.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-medefaidri: Tilt Neon has a splayed c terminal and tube-like strokes of constant width, with a large x-height and short ascenders. Noto Sans Medefaidrin rises high with no ink pooling in its turns.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-mende-kika: Stencil-cut boldness, with a splayed c terminal. Tilt Neon earns its keep big and brief, while the sans-serif Noto Sans Mende Kikakui keeps daylight showing through every curved opening.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-nandinagar: Approachable Noto Sans Nandinagari keeps its openings generous at every weight. Tilt Neon is the loud one, stencil-cut from strokes of a single weight, while the body quietly carries the reading.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-nushu: Noto Sans Nushu towers in the lowercase, its terminals held far from the stroke body. Noto Sans Nushu handles the quiet lines of text, leaving Tilt Neon to be a plain stripe of constant ink.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-old-italic: Noto Sans Old Italic reads compactly, its lowercase nearly as tall as the capitals. Tilt Neon holds tubelike, constant-weight lines up top, and the body keeps curve endings well apart, so paragraphs stay legible.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-old-north-: Rounded and rope-like on top, dense and tall below. Tilt Neon cuts its strokes like lengths of cord, while the terminals of Noto Sans Old North Arabian point outward like tongs, and that clash is the draw.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-oriya: Tilt Neon keeps every letter free of stroke contrast, bold and tube-like with a splayed c terminal. Noto Sans Oriya takes over below with generous curve gaps, its small letters almost as tall as the capitals.
gen-gf-tilt-neon-gf-noto-sans-pahawh-hmo: A splayed c terminal gives Tilt Neon its signature, along with strokes of constant width and a large x-height. Noto Sans Pahawh Hmong echoes that height, the real link between them.
